how: A local server answered www.example.com and api.example.com (one site) and www.example.net (another), mapped to 127.0.0.1 with --host-resolver-rules, over HTTPS with HTTP/2 or with HTTP/1.1 only, and Chrome took its certificate as a site's, by its key (--ignore-certificate-errors-spki-list): it sends a request over an HTTP/2 connection to another name only on a certificate without errors. The server numbered every connection it accepted and kept each request as the bytes said it, with the connection it came on and whether that connection resumed a TLS session. Each scenario ran in a fresh profile, from a page that went on to the run page two seconds after it had loaded: Chrome closes every connection it is not using whenever its certificate verifier is told something new, several times in the moments after it starts. The run page's script called fetch() or sent an XHR, of each credentials mode, to the page's origin, another origin of its site and another site, with preflights, redirects, and connections the server ended after an answer. The run page and the requests after it are kept, but for the page saying it is done and any favicon; the connections are numbered from the run page's, in the order requests first came on them, and the port numbers are left out.
